Key points for the decision
1. The number to book
Hold roughly 390,148,900 in IBNR reserves on this basis. This is the Blended (credibility-weighted) estimate, which keeps standard Chain Ladder for mature periods but anchors the newest, most volatile periods to a stable prior. Plain Chain Ladder alone gives 835,532,148 (a reduction of 445,383,247).
2. Why we don't just use Chain Ladder
Chain Ladder is dependable for older periods but unstable for the newest ones, because it scales a tiny, noisy latest figure up by the full remaining development pattern. The least-developed periods here are 2023-12-01 (10% developed), 2023-11-01 (29% developed), 2023-10-01 (43% developed). These carry most of the estimate's uncertainty and are where the blend does its work; treat their raw CL numbers with caution.
3. The range of outcomes (capital / risk margin)
Simulation puts the central estimate near 721,286,152, with a 1-in-4 adverse outcome around 759,119,756 and a 1-in-20 adverse outcome around 802,677,193. The gap between the central and stress figures is the cushion to weigh when setting risk margin or capital.
4. How much to trust the model
Back-testing on recently held-back data shows strong reliability (average error 3.3%, and a net bias of 2.2% versus actuals). The model has predicted recent actuals closely, which supports confidence in the headline numbers.
5. Timing / cash-flow consideration
Payments peak in Dec (index 243) and trough in Jan (index 76) - a 167-point swing around the average.
6. Method agreement
Across all methods tried, total IBNR ranges over about 591,956,284 (roughly 151.7% of the recommended figure). The methods disagree materially - the final number is sensitive to method choice and warrants explicit sign-off.
Figures reflect the current filter and settings. Adjust the prior, credibility steepness, and seasonality toggle in the sidebar to test sensitivity. This summary is decision support, not a substitute for actuarial sign-off.
